attribution_conclusion.grow_only: Opt-in: no demonstrated incremental benefit; its median was slightly slower with overlapping ranges. Retaining prior high-water vector objects is not justified as a default by this evidence.
attribution_conclusion.palette: Enabled: exact scaled-alpha representation substantially reduces graph storage. The incremental timing attribution is noisy.
attribution_conclusion.positive_quad_add: Enabled: dominant baseline hotspot, exact-bit helper tests, full native/direct regression coverage, and measured combined-default comparison. No claim of an independently resolved gain from the short attribution alone.
attribution_conclusion.scalar_reuse: Enabled: removes measured repeated GMP scalar allocations while retaining only a few scalar objects per thread. The incremental timing gain is unresolved.

contract.floating_exception_flags: Outside the value-equivalence contract: the integer specialization may omit FE_INEXACT while preserving the rounded binary128 value.
contract.preserved: Point identities, loop/regulator order, graph weights, all native scientific output values and promotion counts.

headline: The released default has no resolved serial runtime improvement. Median integration times are about 5% lower at two and four threads and about 4% lower at eight threads, with overlapping timing ranges at four and eight threads. Median peak RSS is 14.6–16.3% lower across the measured thread counts.
historical_comparison_limit: The historical grow-enabled snapshot used an earlier native driver and a separate measurement window. Grow retention, telemetry/code layout, CPU scheduling and other window-dependent effects are confounded. Its 15.9% serial throughput gain is not a demonstrated gain for the released default and must not be attributed solely to grow retention.

historical_grow_enabled.label: historical_combined_grow_enabled
historical_grow_enabled.resource_note: wait4 measures each native child's own CPU and peak RSS. CPU seconds include graph loading and output; CPU/integration-wall is therefore an approximate upper bound on CPU concurrency during integration. Affinity IDs are available logical CPUs, not a count of dedicated physical cores.
historical_grow_enabled.schedule_inference: Near-full task wall occupancy with lower CPU concurrency and many involuntary switches at high thread counts is consistent with scheduling/preemption constraints; the benchmark does not identify a particular quota or hardware topology.

scope_limits: Three counterbalanced repetitions provide measured ranges, not a formal confidence interval.
Hard graph and promotion strata are useful for regressions and hotspot diagnosis; their runtime mix differs from a complete production campaign.
An available affinity set is not evidence of exclusive physical cores; high-thread-count gains must be interpreted with child CPU and context-switch evidence.
Peak RSS includes allocator/library/process overhead; cumulative GMP allocation traffic is not resident memory.
status_meaning: Passed means all planned scientific equality, workload identity and resource-record checks passed. It does not assert a resolved speed improvement at every thread count.
